title: Rivergate and Escarpment
premise: Orsen Vasquez has spent five years as a freelance river surveyor, outrunning the shadow of her famous archaeologist mother and a family scandal she refuses to name. When a flood on the Rivergate exposes a sealed chest bearing the seal of Karvath — a nation erased from every map sixty years ago — she is blackmailed into joining her mother's last-chance expedition before the concession permits expire in ninety days. As the team digs toward an erased city beneath the escarpment, Orsen discovers the find could restore Karvath's descendants' land claims, but only if the truth surfaces before the permits lapse — while her mother plans to bury it forever to protect the team from a vengeful ministry. In the climax, Orsen chooses truth over loyalty, flooding her mother's cover-up with evidence at the exact hour the permits expire; the expedition returns home stripped of glory but having given a dead nation back its name, and Orsen finally measures her life in years instead of miles.
about_author: Dominic Marchetti is a former river barge pilot who spent a decade working the freight lines between forgotten river towns before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who measure their lives in water levels, border crossings, and the things they refuse to say out loud.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Own Books
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Working a survey contract on the Rivergate, she notes an anomaly in the flood-scoured bank — a corner of lacquered wood, stamped metal. She pockets one coin-sized token rather than report it, a small theft that feels like the only honest thing she's done in years. Emotional beat: restless competence masking avoidance.

chapters.title: A Dead Nation's Seal
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. An antiquities broker identifies her token as Karvathi — a nation scrubbed from maps and records after a border war. Within a day, a ministry letter and a private summons arrive; someone is watching her. Emotional beat: the past she fled has found a forwarding address.

chapters.title: The Mother Problem
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, flashback woven in. The private summons is from Dr. Ilse Vasquez — her estranged mother — whose concession permits expire in ninety days. Ilse offers Orsen the surveyor's post she's uniquely qualified for, and implies the ministry will ruin her if she refuses. Emotional beat: resentment sharpened into wary negotiation.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She signs on, telling herself it's for the money. At the expedition's staging camp below the escarpment she meets the team: a loyal foreman, a nervous cartographer, and a ministry observer named Dallet who smiles too easily. Emotional beat: belonging offered on suspicious terms.

chapters.title: What the Flood Gave Up
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Her instruments confirm a buried structure beneath the escarpment's talus — far larger than Ilse's published theory allows. Ilse quietly redirects the dig away from the strongest readings. Emotional beat: first crack in trust; Orsen realizes her mother is managing the truth, not seeking it.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Doubt
chapters.summary: Sef the cartographer's POV. Sef has noticed the survey maps don't match the field notes and brings his worry to Orsen. Together they find Ilse has been logging false coordinates. Emotional beat: complicity offered; the loyalty-vs-truth theme turns personal.

chapters.title: Dallet's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The ministry observer invites Orsen to dinner and reveals he knows about the token she kept — and about her mother's falsified logs. He offers protection in exchange for reporting everything. Emotional beat: blackmail wearing a friendly face; Orsen sees she's a piece on two boards.

chapters.title: Down Through the Talus
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Against Ilse's wishes, Orsen runs a night survey that confirms an entrance shaft. The crew breaks through into a corridor of Karvathi masonry — and wall inscriptions naming living descendant villages that still exist downriver. Emotional beat: awe colliding with dread of what the discovery demands.

chapters.title: The Descendants
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A delegation from the Karvathi-descendant river villages arrives at camp, led by a schoolteacher named Maren, asking one question: did you find proof we were here? Ilse stonewalls them. Emotional beat: Orsen sees her own rootlessness mirrored in people who lost a homeland on paper.

chapters.title: Ilse's Version
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reveals her reasoning: publishing now, under a hostile ministry, means the find is seized, the team prosecuted, and the site sealed — possibly destroyed. Silence protects the dig and the descendants' eventual claim. Emotional beat: her cover-up reframed as sacrifice; Orsen almost believes her.

chapters.title: The Permit Clock
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Thirty days remain. Dallet pressures Orsen for the falsified logs; Maren's villagers begin a quiet vigil at the camp's edge; Sef wavers under ministry threats to his family. Emotional beat: every loyalty now has a price tag.

chapters.title: The Second Chest
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Digging deeper, the team opens a second chamber containing the Karvathi national archive — census rolls, land grants, names. It is everything the descendants need. Ilse orders it sealed and unlogged. Emotional beat: wonder curdling; the truth now physically exists and is being buried a second time.

chapters.title: Sef Breaks
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Cornered by Dallet, Sef hands over copies of the false maps — omitting, deliberately, the archive chamber. Orsen learns of the betrayal and must decide whether to expose him. Emotional beat: forgiveness tested against the expedition's survival.

chapters.title: The Vigil
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The villagers' vigil grows; Dallet moves to clear them by force. Orsen stands between the ministry men and the schoolteacher, and the moment is photographed by a camp hand. Emotional beat: Orsen stops being a bystander to history and becomes part of it.

chapters.title: Ilse and Orsen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mother and daughter finally speak plainly: about the old scandal, about Ilse's career built partly on a suppressed Karvathi dig twenty years ago, about why silence became her religion. Emotional beat: the estrangement explained, not excused; love and betrayal sharing a room.

chapters.title: Dallet Moves
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With ten days left, Dallet files to revoke the concession early, citing falsified records — using Sef's maps. If the permits die before the truth surfaces, the site is sealed and the archive lost indefinitely. Emotional beat: the trap closes; the law itself becomes the weapon against justice.

chapters.title: The Long Night Survey
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen, Sef seeking redemption, and two loyal crew members secretly photograph and copy the entire archive through the night, racing Dallet's inspection team. Emotional beat: exhausted, conspiratorial hope — the expedition finally working as one, for something larger than itself.

chapters.title: The Inspection
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Dallet arrives to seal the site. Ilse, to Orsen's shock, stalls him with a flawless performance — protecting the dig while still refusing to publish. Orsen realizes her mother will never choose truth on her own. Emotional beat: heartbreak as clarity.

chapters.title: Permits Expire
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The final day. As the concession legally lapses at midnight, Orsen releases the archive copies, the photographs, and the true survey to the descendants, the press, and the ministry's own oversight board — simultaneously, so no one can bury it. Emotional beat: the point of no return, chosen freely.

chapters.title: What the Mother Said
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Confronted with the release, Ilse rages, then breaks: she signs a sworn statement corroborating the find, surrendering her career to save her daughter from prosecution. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth reconciled at last, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In the river villages, the census rolls are read aloud — every name of the erased nation, spoken publicly for the first time in sixty years. Land claims are filed; the site is protected as heritage, not seized. Emotional beat: grief and restoration in the same breath.

chapters.title: Miles Into Years
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Months later, Orsen takes a contract surveying the Rivergate again — but this time she stays in one town, teaches Maren's students to read instruments, and visits her mother under supervision of her appeals. She measures her life in seasons now. Emotional beat: belonging earned, the river finally home.
